# `silk/time/zones_bundle`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A `TimeZones` provider over the bytes of a time zone bundle: one file with every zone of a
release of the IANA time zone database.

## When to use

Use [`ZoneBundle`](#ZoneBundle) in a program that ships or downloads its own bundle, for example a newer
release than the one inside the standard library. Use `BundledTimeZones` of
`silk.time.zones_bundled` for the bundle that the standard library carries, and `OsTimeZones`
of `silk.time.zones_native` for the zones of the operating system.

## Details

A bundle is the file that `scripts/time/generate-tzdb` of the Silk repository writes. It
holds the names of all zones and links, one TZif file for each distinct zone, the name of the
release, and the table that maps the zone names of Windows to IANA names.
[`ZoneBundle.fromBytes`](#ZoneBundle.impl.fromBytes) checks the tables one time, and a lookup then reads only the entry
and the TZif file of one zone.

## Examples

### Read a zone from a bundle file

```silk,ignore
import silk.build.source { Source }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.time.zone { Zone }
import silk.time.zones { TimeZones, ZoneLookupError }
import silk.time.zones_bundle { ZoneBundle }

effect fn rome() -> Zone ! ZoneLookupError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut zones = run ZoneBundle.fromBytes(Source.read("data/tzdb.bin"))
  return run TimeZones.zone("Europe/Rome") |> Effect.provideMut<TimeZones>(&mut zones)
}
```

Import as `ZoneBundle` with `import silk.time.zones_bundle { ZoneBundle }`.

## `ZoneBundle`

```silk
pub struct ZoneBundle
```

A `TimeZones` provider over the bytes of one time zone bundle. It owns the bytes.

### Details

The provider gives every zone and link of the bundle, and `UTC` and fixed offsets as every
provider does. Names are compared without letter case, and a zone has the name as the bundle
spells it. [`ZoneBundle.windowsZone`](#ZoneBundle.impl.windowsZone) gives the IANA name for a zone name of Windows.

<a id="ZoneBundle.impl.fromBytes"></a>

### Associated function `fromBytes`

```silk
pub effect fn fromBytes(data: &[u8]) -> ZoneBundle ! ZoneLookupError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a provider over a copy of the bundle `data`.

#### Errors

- `ZoneLookupError` with the reason `InvalidData` if `data` is not a bundle or one of its
  tables points outside the data.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the copy.

<a id="ZoneBundle.impl.fromOwned"></a>

### Associated function `fromOwned`

```silk
pub effect fn fromOwned(data: Bytes) -> ZoneBundle ! ZoneLookupError
```

Returns a provider over the bundle `data`, which it takes over without a copy.

#### Errors

- `ZoneLookupError` with the reason `InvalidData` if `data` is not a bundle or one of its
  tables points outside the data.

<a id="ZoneBundle.impl.windowsZone"></a>

### Method `windowsZone`

```silk
pub fn windowsZone(self: &Self, name: &[u8]) -> Option<&[u8]>
```

Returns the IANA zone name for the zone name of Windows `name`, such as `Europe/Berlin`
for `W. Europe Standard Time`, or `None` if the bundle does not list the name. Letter case
does not matter.

#### Details

The table is the one of the Unicode CLDR project, with the default zone of each Windows
name.

<a id="ZoneBundle.impl.nameCount"></a>

Returns the number of zone names in the bundle, with the links.
